findings.note: The PowerShell twin conflates 'supplied but empty' with 'omitted'. With -CapabilityReasons '' the entire fragment block is skipped: no read, no shape check, no exit 2. The bash twin for the identical invocation sets capability_reasons_supplied=1 and raises OSError, printing the fragment-invalid diagnostic and exiting 2. Contradicts requirements.md Security Boundaries ('The only condition that legitimately degrades rather than Blocks is the second argument's own total absence') and AC-027. It is the exact fail-open Blocker [B3]/INV-014 was raised to close, on a Security-Sensitive/high gate. No fixture covers it: TEST-013a-g test only missing/malformed/missing-key/non-array/missing-id/missing-eligible/omitted.

findings.ref: sh: if not isinstance(reasons, list): raise ValueError('upgrade_reasons is not an array') vs ps1: $reasons = @($entry.upgrade_reasons)
findings.note: The ps1 twin omits the array-type validation the sh twin performs. For a fragment entry whose upgrade_reasons is a scalar, bash exits 2 while PowerShell wraps it with @(...), emits it as a trigger token and exits 10. The two runtimes return different exit codes and different stdout for byte-identical input on a gate whose exit code decides Lite vs full. AC-027 requires exit 2; no TEST-013 fixture in either runtime exercises a non-array upgrade_reasons, so the asymmetry is invisible to the 43/43 GREEN evidence.

findings.ref: sh: if entry['eligible'] is False, ps1: if ($entry.eligible -eq $false), design.md API/Contract Plan 'where entry[eligible] == false', Field Definitions
findings.note: Neither twin validates the type of eligible or id; both only check key presence. (a) eligible:null passes presence on BOTH runtimes and contributes nothing, so a shape-invalid fragment silently yields lite-eligible exit 0 - the silent degrade AC-027 forbids for a supplied fragment. (b) eligible:0 or 'false' diverges between twins: Python 'is False' is identity so bash treats it as eligible (fail-open), PowerShell '-eq $false' coerces and exits 10. (c) sh's 'is False' is drift from design.md's stated '== false'. (d) id is emitted with no non-empty-string check into the output grammar 'full-required: <primary-id>; triggers=<ordered-ids>' and can inject , or ; into the field callers parse.

findings.ref: human-copy README 'What's staged' vs AC-010 and tasks.md T-002 Planned Files
findings.note: AC-010 requires the human-copy payload set to be exactly the four declared targets. The delivered directory also contains .github/workflows/test.yml (a T-002 Planned File) and README.md, and the README states both are NOT control files by INV-020, so Get-PayloadFileSet enumerates them and Test-ExactSet rejects the batch. T-002's Done-When HUMAN APPLY STEP cannot succeed without an out-of-band rm that appears nowhere in tasks.md. The README also records tasks.md Protected Files item 3 as an acknowledged, still-unresolved spec self-contradiction resolved by implementer interpretation.

findings.ref: tasks.md T-002 Blocker note vs human-copy README 'Canonical-path staging (current)'
findings.note: The frozen Blocker note still describes the payload as staged under human-copy/PROPOSED/ with its own README. The README states that subtree was migrated to canonical paths and deleted. The task contract text a reviewer is told to check against is stale relative to the delivered state.

The comment asserts both 'Recorded honestly as passes:false -- this is why the contract currently FAILS overall' and, appended, 'It is now passes:true, re-recorded 2026-08-19'. The artifact is internally self-contradictory about its own verdict.

findings.ref: T-002.contract.json regression check (required:true, passes:true) vs its comment
findings.note: regression is recorded as a passing required check while the comment states the full 116-suite run TIMED OUT after 10 minutes, and the repository-state section reports exit 1 with 97/102 suites passed. The scoping is disclosed honestly but the check as recorded overstates what was executed.

findings.ref: tasks.md T-002 Done-When: CHANGELOG '## Unreleased' entry citing #194; grep self-check on version strings
findings.note: Stated explicitly as unverifiable from the bundle alone: no CHANGELOG text, no Unreleased #194 entry body, and no grep self-check command or output appears anywhere. By contrast the three MANIFEST.sha256 entries and the four CI steps this Done-When also requires ARE present and checkable.

findings.ref: Bundle self-inclusion: embedded cross-model-verdict/v1 for sibling task T-001 and whole-bundle duplication
findings.note: Sanitization defect in the panelist input bundle itself: it embeds a complete prior cross-model verdict (sibling task T-001, same vendor slot), leaking prior-reviewer conclusions into a bundle whose header declares a blind review. Detected via a key-only grep and not read further. The bundle body is also duplicated verbatim, inflating it to 1.3 MB.

findings.ref: tasks.md T-002 'Cross-Model: not enabled' vs bundle header '# consent: sudo'
findings.note: The frozen task contract declares cross-model verification as not enabled, so this panel's verdict has no declared consumer in the task contract. The header records sudo consent, so the run may be authorized out-of-band, but the two disagree and one should be reconciled before the verdict is relied on.
